purpose: Hypothesis falsification / evidence closure: counterbalanced slider probes identified from EXISTING data, and B2 dense candidate-mechanism elimination. No human answers were collected for these probes.

hypotheses.H_distance: players judge the slider question mainly by slider path/follow DISTANCE
hypotheses.H_duration: players judge mainly by per-slider follow DURATION / time tail

dense_b2_candidate_elimination.composite_observation: On pairs where one side is clearly faster AND denser (peak 1s rate and object frequency well separated), humans follow the faster side (263cea7e, 2bd327, 8f60b830, a933aa2d, d545e72e); where both sides are slow (peak rate <=4: B2 and 4319b133), humans fall back to sustained-rhythm structure (beat-relative runs), consistent with the question wording '连续快速点击' (fast AND continuous). One EQUAL case (891c407b) is violated by every single candidate. This composite is a hypothesis over n=9 directional cases, not a proof.
dense_b2_candidate_elimination.verdict_on_b2: Still MISSING_OBSERVABLE: the code observes none of the viable candidate observables for this pair; no single mechanism is uniquely identified and none is declared a winner.

follow_duration_derivability.q1_detail: HitObject.time_ms is the start; the normalized layer exposes canonical_end_time_ms() = time_ms + slider_total_duration_ms; slider_total_duration_ms = single_span_duration_ms * span_count (span_count = max(1, parsed_slides); repeat_count = span_count - 1)
follow_duration_derivability.q2_detail: parse_osu_file + normalize (project parser, unchanged) yields per-slider slider_total_duration_ms; segment aggregates (p90/median/max over sliders whose start falls inside the canonical 5 s segment) were computed for 31,821 segments by tmp/gap_audit/find_counterbalanced_probes_v01.py
follow_duration_derivability.q3_repeat_duration_semantics: full traversal across every span; ball follows span_count passes in the renderer, so total duration is the visual follow time
follow_duration_derivability.q3_formula: single_span = pixel_length / (SliderMultiplier * 100 * SV) * beat_length_ms (osu formula, normalized layer); contract form: path_distance / velocity; total = single_span * span_count
follow_duration_derivability.q4_speed_mods: current scope is NM-only (no mod input anywhere in the pipeline; the presentation always shows NM). If mods ever enter: effective duration = raw_total_duration / speed_multiplier (DT 1.5, HT 0.75); which duration to present must be an explicit contract decision, not silently mixed
follow_duration_derivability.q5_detail: Local signal v0.3 already computes per-row ls.slider_total_duration_ms AND ls.lazy_travel_time_ms (tracking time incl. late tick before tail reorder); the slider_control_load proposition consumes map-level slider.duration_ms_p90; the slider_tracking rule consumes ONLY ls.lazy_travel_distance_cs_normalised p90. The time-domain fields exist in the same layer but are not rule inputs
follow_duration_derivability.q6_why_segment_max_exists_but_unused: it is carried from the Local source's segment summary via context.provenance['source_segment_max'] and echoed as a diagnostic; the v0.1 rule's declared discriminator consumes only p90 (>=100 positive, max==0 negative, else abstain). The only on-record rationale is the documented failure mode 'segment p90 can hide one extreme slider' plus the pilot rule policy 'Thresholds are sparse QA discriminators, not learned boundaries'
follow_duration_derivability.q7_exact_p90_failure_mode_for_extreme_sl: p90 is the 90th-percentile row of per-row lazy travel distance (non-slider rows are zero). A single extreme slider lies ABOVE p90: its magnitude is not reflected in the p90 value, only whether it shifts the 90% boundary. The rule therefore cannot distinguish 'one monster slider among short ones' from 'uniformly long sliders' — exactly the B4/B5/B6 situation (segment_max 188.4 vs 114.2 hidden behind p90 108.767 vs 108.768)
